body: Host restarted with cargo run (observed by Opus2 on 2026-10-05 at 03:08Z; recorded by Fable2; a supplement to landing-integration-and-install, BUILD AND INSTALL, which is at its size limit). Greg's restart ran `cargo run --release` in the master checkout. Cargo RELINKED target/release/termal.exe in place from master's source, at 03:10:35Z. That overwrote the binary the integration owner had installed (8e4f4e30; the new hash is 6897a1bb) and broke the .bak chain. A byte compare against the clean-export build of the same commit differed only in the PE link timestamp, three debug-directory stamps and the 16-byte PDB GUID. So after such a restart: (1) do not treat the hash change as unauthorised; verify that the code is equivalent to the landed commit by that byte compare, and record the new hash; (2) keep the clean-export build output (.tmp/install-target or target/release-clean-<sha>) as the backup, since the in-place .bak may be gone; (3) master must be clean at the landed commit before any restart, because cargo builds whatever the master checkout holds.
